title: BOJ seen hiking to 1.25pct in September as yen weakness accelerates timeline
body: The sharp shift in economist expectations points to a BOJ that is now genuinely behind the curve on tightening, with the terminal rate view moving higher and the timeline compressing in the space of a single month. For yen crosses, this raises the stakes around the September meeting considerably, since a hike is now largely priced and any delay risks a disorderly reaction given how quickly consensus has moved. At the same time, the poll's finding that last month's coordinated intervention was largely ineffective suggests the yen remains vulnerable to renewed selling pressure regardless of what the BOJ does, particularly if Takaichi's fiscal plans proceed without clear funding. Traders will likely treat the September decision as a binary event risk for JPY pairs, with confirmation of a hike doing less to support the yen than a surprise hold would do to weaken it further. --- September in close to being locked in: BOJ likely to hike next month and again in January, says ex-board member MUFG sees yen risk skewed weaker despite 80% BOJ hike odds --- The BOJ has gone from an outside chance of a September hike to the consensus view in the space of one month, and economists still don't think it will be enough to save the yen.

title: Mexican Peso holds below 16.95 as traders eye US data, Iran shift
body: The Mexican Peso holds firm near 10-year highs against the US Dollar on Tuesday, as the USD/MXN pair sits below the 16.95 level while investors digest US economic data and recent developments between the US and Iran. The exotic pair trades at 16.94, virtually unchanged.
